## Bhagavad Gita on endurance

Bhagavad Gita (Received form c. 2nd century BCE – 2nd century CE) approaches endurance within Indian Classical Philosophy. The argument turns on the distinction between action and its fruits. Arjuna's objection is that acting will make him complicit in slaughter; Kṛṣṇa's answer is not that the slaughter is permissible but that Arjuna has misdescribed the self that would be doing it. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets endurance most directly—useful for searches such as “bhagavad gita quotes on endurance.”
